agents.name: Kira
agents.description: Writes the proposals and the case studies

messages.text: Clara, I have been heads-down on delivery for three weeks. Where is the pipeline?
Here it is: **£41,500 open** across four conversations, plus one invoice that is late. Two of them need you this week.

What I would do, in order:

1. Send the cycle-hire co-op their contract today. That is money already won.
2. Answer the harbour museum. They asked a question on Tuesday and nobody replied.
3. Nudge the bakery group with something useful, not "just checking in".
Ouch on the museum. What did they ask?

Whether the price includes training their front-of-house team. It does: two sessions, and it is on page four of the proposal. I have drafted a reply that quotes that line, so it reads as clarity and not as a concession.
The case study for the cycle-hire co-op is drafted: 600 words, one chart, and their quote at the top. Clara, it should help with the bakery.
It will. Second sites are exactly what the bakery group is worried about. I will use it.
Invoice 2041 is fourteen days late, £3,200. Second reminder sent this morning, politely.
The school trust proposal is outlined. I need your day rate for the workshop before I can finish the pricing page.
September invoicing is out: six invoices, £21,400 in total. Five are already paid.

present.draft: Send it. And write me the bakery nudge.

toolCall.title: Reading the thread
toolCall.output: Last reply 16 days ago. They mentioned opening a fourth shop in March.

reply.text:
The museum reply is sent.

For the bakery, this is the nudge:

*You mentioned the fourth shop opens in March. In case it helps, here is the short case study from when the cycle-hire co-op opened their second site: what they had live on day one, and what could wait. No strings; it made me think of you.*

It gives them something, it shows you listened about March, and it asks for nothing. Shall I send it from you?
Invoice 2041 was paid this morning, £3,200. September is now fully collected.
